Consult Summary:
23-year-old female with 3–4-day history of constant, worsening mid-lower abdominal pain (8/10) associated with light post-menstrual vaginal spotting and nausea. No red-flag systemic features. Face-to-face abdominal exam and repeat pregnancy test arranged.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute lower abdominal pain
- Onset: “few days ago”; constant, worsening; severity 8/10.
- Location: central lower abdomen, below umbilicus.
- Associated positives: light pink vaginal bleeding after menses, nausea without vomiting, mild non-offensive vaginal discharge.
- Associated negatives: fever, shoulder pain, dyspnea, syncope, urinary frequency/odor/pain, weight loss, blood in stool/urine.
- Gynecologic history: Last menstrual period 2–3 weeks ago (normal). Sexually active; last intercourse 4 days ago. Etonogestrel implant placed 1 year ago. Last pregnancy test 1 month ago (negative). No prior pregnancies.
- Differential discussed: pregnancy-related pain (including ectopic), gynecological or gastrointestinal causes.
- Plan: Arrange urgent face-to-face abdominal examination; patient to perform home urine pregnancy test today and call immediately if positive or if pain worsens/vomiting/fluids not tolerated.

Issue 2: Recent constipation
- Constipation for one week last week; bowel habit now normal. No current diarrhea or hard stools.
- Monitoring only unless symptoms recur.

Issue 3: Drug allergy
- History of allergy to amoxicillin (reaction details not specified).

Medications:
- Etonogestrel implant (Implanon), dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin (reaction not detailed).

Past Medical History:
- No past surgeries or chronic illnesses reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: school teacher.
- Lives with husband and husband’s family.
- Smoking: denies.
- Alcohol: not documented (patient unclear).
- Recreational drugs: denies.
- Recent travel: abroad 1 year ago; none recently.

Preventative History:
- No information provided on cervical screening, vaccinations, or other preventive care.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or physical exam performed in telehealth consult.

Plan:
- Patient to phone support line today to schedule same-day/next-day in-person abdominal and possibly pelvic examination.
- Perform urine pregnancy test today; if positive or if pain or vomiting worsens/unable to tolerate fluids, patient to seek urgent care.
- Provide safety-net advice as above.
- No medications prescribed pending examination.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing expected elements:
  – Vitals, abdominal/pelvic examination findings, full medication reconciliation, detailed allergy reaction, alcohol quantity, gynecologic history (pap smear), vaccination status.

● Internal conflicts: none noted.

● Transcript quality: clear overall; occasional audio gaps but clinical content understandable.
